$comment: exceptions[]: components whose license is NOT on the allowlist (tools/licensing/policy.json); each references an ADR. copyleftGate[]: allowlisted but copyleft components (e.g. MPL-2.0) that must stay tracked. Every copyleft entry carries a gate status; 'spike-only, gate pending' means a compliance ADR is required before it ships (ADR-0008, Copyleft adoption gate). Matching is by ecosystem + name + license + scope, so a license change upstream re-opens the question.

exceptions.name: YARC-Official/YARG.Core
exceptions.reason: S2/S3 spike harnesses fetch YARG.Core at a pinned commit (S2) or as the fork's submodule (S3) into gitignored external/ folders and build against it. Nothing is vendored; the harness source stays MIT.
exceptions.revisit: Never vendor. Any shipped use needs a compliance ADR (ADR-0008 Copyleft adoption gate); ADR-0004 already rules out a product dependency on YARG.

exceptions.name: dcuccia/YARG (branch handbell-spike)
exceptions.reason: The YARG fork (community track, ADR-0004) is fetched by S3's harness and by tools/setup/setup-yarg.ps1; it lives in its own LGPL repository.
exceptions.revisit: Author fork code here first (MIT) and contribute it outbound, per ADR-0008.

exceptions.name: spikes/s2-yarg-core/patches/0001-yarglogger-no-thread-on-browser.diff
exceptions.reason: Owner decision 2026-10-23: keep. A unified diff against YARG.Core's YargLogger.cs; its context lines are YARG.Core code, so the file is LGPL-3.0-or-later (notice header + REUSE.toml), not MIT.
exceptions.revisit: Upstream the fix (draft issue in the S2 report) and then delete the patch.

copyleftGate.name: mediabunny
copyleftGate.reason: Optional transitive dependency of werift (S1's WebRTC DataChannel experiment), used unmodified from npm and not bundled into any web page.
copyleftGate.revisit: Before shipping WebRTC via werift: compliance ADR (notices; publish any modified MPL files), or choose a WebRTC path without it.
